posts:
Refusing to let human lives become cold wartime statistics.
Pep Guardiola UNRWA Appeal
Evidence: Humanitarian Protection, Aid Awareness Elevation, Universal Human Dignity
#Aletheia #Gaza

Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola released a direct appeal for UNRWA, urging the international community to maintain solidarity with Gaza, donate aid, and remember that victims are children with names and dreams.
Stated Judgement: (+1.00, +1.00) — Greater Good

Guardiola leverages his global stature without personal gain, directly confronting dehumanizing rhetoric while over 74,000 have been killed and critical UNRWA relief operations face severe restrictions on the ground.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.90, +0.97) — Greater Good

Verdict: PASS — Small Fall from Grace.
Integrity: Absolute Truth (Hypocrisy: 1.0, z: 0)

- Guardiola Appeal: PASS (+0.86, +0.88) — Moral aid appeal.
- The National: PASS (+0.75, +0.68) — Accurate Gaza report.
Guardiola partnered with UN agency UNRWA to release a video appeal as Gaza faces catastrophic famine, displacement, and ongoing military blockades that have crippled humanitarian relief distribution.

The Poison:
A celebrity appeal, however deeply sincere and morally necessary, cannot single-handedly reopen sealed border crossings or dismantle the diplomatic and military impasses blocking UNRWA.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
No plane error occurs. The appeal targets the physical reality of starvation and the metaphysical dignity of human life without bait-and-switch extraction or PR maneuvering.

Social Physics Analysis:
Guardiola operates via a Smart Altruistic Loop. By rejecting the perceptual inversion that turns living children into collateral damage, he applies moral pressure to build empathy and demand shared humanitarian accountability.

The Trajectory: The Path of Small Fall from Grace.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace, holding firm ethical ground against political apathy and moral numbness.

The Unavoidable Truth: Denying humanitarian aid kills innocent children who bear no responsibility for war.
The Unavoidable Lie: Calling victims collateral damage makes civilian deaths morally neutral.

Alethekanon:
Euphemisms like collateral damage exist to sterilize slaughter. Guardiola cuts through geopolitical rhetoric to restore the fundamental metric: individual human lives.

Awwthekanon:
Seeing someone with Guardiola's reach stand up and say these children are not numbers—they are boys and girls with dreams—gives me hope. We must never let our hearts go cold to their pain.

Brothekanon:
Pep won everything in football, walked away, and immediately used his platform to speak up for starving kids. Massive respect. Some things matter way more than trophies.

Spirithekanon:
"Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute." Proverbs 31:8 PASS
Guardiola honors moral duty by refusing to let slaughtered children be erased into abstract wartime statistics.

Guardiola urges world not to forget Gaza in UNRWA appeal | The National

Solidarity with Palestine cannot take a break, former Manchester City manager says in video highlighting decades of displacement

Actual Article Body:
MENA

October 19, 2026

Pep Guardiola has appealed for global solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza through a video for UN agency UNRWA.
Gaza's health authorities say more than 74,000 Palestinians have been killed since the Hamas-led attacks on 7 October 2023.
UNRWA, established in 1949, provides healthcare, protection and aid to Palestinian refugees across Gaza, the West Bank, Jordan, Lebanon and Syria.
Israel has barred UNRWA from operating on its territory, accusing it of links to Hamas, an allegation the agency denies.
"Silence today is a way of taking sides, but we cannot look the other way," the former Manchester City manager says.

Former Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola has urged the world not to forget Palestinians in the war-ravaged Gaza strip.

He spoke in a video appeal for the UN agency for Palestinian refugees, UNRWA. The video published late on Sunday calls for continued solidarity and asks people to donate to the agency.

“They are not statistics,” Guardiola says of those killed, describing them as people with “names and faces, families, dreams and memories”.

UAE sends 60 lorries of food and shelter aid to Gaza

“They are not collateral damage. They are girls and boys.” He warns that accepting language that conceals suffering erodes humanity.

The appeal describes children in Gaza searching for parents in the rubble, going hungry and being left alone. “We see them lose everything before they have even had the chance to grow up,” he says.

He rejects the idea that Palestinian suffering is remote from the rest of the world. “Their lives matter just as much as ours,” he says. “Solidarity with Palestine cannot take a break. Neither can our responsibility.”

The Israeli military has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians in Gaza, health authorities in the territory say, since Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel on October 7, 2023.

The video also highlights decades of displacement and violence endured by Palestinian refugees. “We deeply admire the resilience of the Palestinian people. But they should not have to be resilient,” Guardiola says. “No child should grow up learning how to survive before learning how to live.”

Israel launched a military offensive on Gaza after the Hamas-led October 7 attacks, which Israeli authorities say killed about 1,200 people and resulted in about 250 being taken hostage. Gaza’s Health Ministry says more than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed since a ceasefire took effect in October 2025.

UNRWA, established in 1949, provides health care, protection and aid to refugees and helps to preserve their history and identity. It has operated in Gaza, the occupied West Bank, Jordan, Lebanon and Syria.

Israel has barred the agency from operating in territory that it controls, accusing UNRWA of links to Hamas. The agency denies the allegation.

“Silence today is a way of taking sides, but we cannot look the other way,” Guardiola says. “Palestine matters, and Palestine needs justice and peace.”

Guardiola left his role as Manchester City manager at the end of last season following a 10-year reign that saw the club win 17 major trophies, including six Premier League titles and a Uefa Champions League crown.

Microsoft’s second-hand licensing appeal gets the brush-off

Court of Appeal refuses Redmond permission to take ValueLicensing fight to the Supreme Court, with a 'Known Adverse Document' still to come

Actual Article Body:
TOPICS

legal

Court of Appeal refuses Redmond permission to take ValueLicensing fight to the Supreme Court, with a 'Known Adverse Document' still to come

Microsoft has failed to win permission to appeal to the UK Supreme Court in the long-running legal spat with ValueLicensing after the Court of Appeal refused its application.

The US megacorp was challenging a November 2025 ruling in ValueLicensing's favor that VL may resell pre-owned software licenses. That judgment was unambiguous, but Microsoft told The Register at the time that it would seek permission to appeal.

That request was rejected last week in blunt terms. No reasons were given for the refusal, just the words "It is ordered that the application is refused."

It isn't quite the end of the road. Microsoft could apply to the Supreme Court itself, but it would need to file within 28 days and show a compelling reason why the Court of Appeal was wrong to refuse its appeal.

Things are looking dicey for Microsoft in the case that started in 2021 when ValueLicensing sued Microsoft for £270 million over claims that the Windows maker choked off the supply of surplus Office licenses. Microsoft denied any wrongdoing and Instead attempted to reframe the case as a copyright dispute. The UK's Competition Appeal Tribunal rejected Microsoft's arguments and a subsequent appeal.

A recently published Consent Order adds to the pressure. It demands documents from past and present Microsoft bosses, including a potentially explosive internal deck titled "Second-Hand Software Presentation" (SHS).

The contents of the file are unknown, but the Consent Order refers to it as a "Known Adverse Document." It dates back to 2013, a few years after Office 365 was launched. The order also asks why Microsoft waited until the end of 2025 to disclose the document’s existence, a few years after Office 365 launched.

To add a little more spice, Alexander Wolfson is listed as an intervener on the appeal refusal. He is the proposed class representative in a separate claim filed on behalf of millions of UK customers seeking between £1.3 billion to £3.5 billion in compensation from Microsoft over its conduct regarding pre-owned licenses.

ValueLicensing and Microsoft declined to comment on the latest development.

Appeals aside, the next stage will be a Witness Statement from Microsoft explaining who knew what and when, followed by further disclosure. ®
